stem: after the Battle of Siffin, the Kharijites (khawarij, "those who went out") left Ali's camp crying "no judgment but God's" (la hukma illa lillah). what were they protesting?
options: his march on Basra against Aisha, Talhah and Zubayr
his agreement to let men arbitrate with Mu'awiyah
his move of the seat of rule from Medina to Kufa
his refusal to hand over the killers of Uthman
why: The Kharijites rejected the arbitration Ali accepted at Siffin, saying judgment belongs to God alone; Ali answered, as Sahih Muslim records, that it was a word of truth by which falsehood was intended.
source: Sahih Muslim, Book of Zakat (on the Kharijites); al-Tabari, History

es.stem: después de la batalla de Siffin, los jariyíes (khawarij, "los que salieron") dejaron el campamento de Ali gritando "no hay juicio sino el de Dios" (la hukma illa lillah). ¿contra qué protestaban?
options: su marcha a Basora contra Aisha, Talhah y Zubayr
su acuerdo de dejar que hombres arbitraran con Muawiya
su traslado de la sede del gobierno de Medina a Kufa
su negativa a entregar a los asesinos de Uthman
es.why: Los jariyíes rechazaron el arbitraje que Ali aceptó en Siffin, diciendo que el juicio pertenece solo a Dios; Ali respondió, como recoge el Sahih Muslim, que era una palabra de verdad con la que se buscaba la falsedad.

stem: Husayn ibn Ali was killed at Karbala on a day already kept with a fast since the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina. which day of the Islamic calendar was it?
options: the first day of Shawwal
the twelfth of Rabi al-Awwal
the tenth day of Muharram
the fifteenth of Sha'ban
why: Husayn was killed on 10 Muharram, the day called Ashura. Bukhari records that the Prophet ﷺ fasted that day in Medina, in memory of God saving Moses (Musa), peace be upon him.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Fasting (Ashura); al-Tabari, History

es.stem: Husayn ibn Ali murió en Karbala en un día que ya se guardaba con ayuno desde que el Profeta ﷺ llegó a Medina. ¿qué día del calendario islámico era?
options: el primer día de Shawwal
el doce de Rabi al-Awwal
el décimo día de Muharram
el decimoquinto de Shaabán
es.why: Husayn murió el 10 de Muharram, el día llamado Ashura. Bukhari recoge que el Profeta ﷺ ayunaba ese día en Medina, en memoria de cuando Dios salvó a Moisés (Musa), la paz sea con él.

stem: a ruler claims a coat of armour (dir') that another man holds; his witnesses are his son and his freed servant. in the well-known report of Caliph Ali before the judge Shurayh, how was the case decided?
options: for the other man, since the son's word for his father was refused
for the caliph, since a ruler's own word needs no further witness
by sending it up to the caliph's council for a final verdict
by splitting the disputed armour between the two men equally
why: In the report, Ali brought his son Hasan and his freed servant Qanbar; Shurayh would not accept a son's testimony for his father, so one witness remained and he ruled for the other man, keeping the Qur'an's command to judge with justice (4:58). The report is in later collections such as al-Bayhaqi's, and its chain is debated.
source: al-Bayhaqi, al-Sunan al-Kubra; Abu Nu'aym, Hilyat al-Awliya; Qur'an 4:58

es.stem: un gobernante reclama una cota de malla (dir') que tiene otro hombre; sus testigos son su hijo y su sirviente liberto. en el conocido relato del califa Ali ante el juez Shurayh, ¿cómo se resolvió el caso?
options: a favor del otro hombre: no se aceptó al hijo por su padre
a favor del califa, pues su palabra no necesita otro testigo
enviándolo al consejo del califa para un veredicto final
repartiendo la cota de malla en disputa entre los dos hombres
es.why: En el relato, Ali presentó a su hijo Hasan y a su sirviente liberto Qanbar; Shurayh no aceptó el testimonio de un hijo a favor de su padre, así que quedó un solo testigo y falló por el otro hombre, cumpliendo el mandato del Corán de juzgar con justicia (4:58). El relato está en colecciones posteriores, como la de al-Bayhaqi, y su cadena se discute.

stem: in his Book of Optics (Kitab al-Manazir), what did Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) of Cairo argue is how we come to see things?
options: rays sent out from the eye reach the things it sees
thin copies shed by things travel into the eye
the eye's rays meet sunlight halfway to the thing
light from each point of a thing enters the eye
why: Against the older view that the eye sends out rays, Ibn al-Haytham argued from experiments, such as lamps casting separate spots of light in a dark room, that light travels in straight lines from each point of an object into the eye.
source: Ibn al-Haytham, Kitab al-Manazir (Book of Optics), Book 1

es.stem: en su Libro de óptica (Kitab al-Manazir), ¿cómo dijo Ibn al-Haytham (Alhacén) de El Cairo que llegamos a ver las cosas?
options: el ojo envía rayos que alcanzan las cosas que ve
copias finas que sueltan las cosas entran al ojo
los rayos del ojo se juntan con la luz del sol
la luz de cada punto de una cosa entra en el ojo
es.why: Frente a la idea antigua de que el ojo envía rayos, Ibn al-Haytham argumentó con experimentos, como lámparas que dejan manchas de luz separadas en un cuarto oscuro, que la luz viaja en línea recta desde cada punto de un objeto hasta el ojo.

stem: in his Decisive Treatise (Fasl al-Maqal), what does Ibn Rushd (Averroes) argue the religious law says about studying philosophy?
options: it forbids it, as reasoning leads believers from faith
it permits it only to rulers and their court doctors
it commands it for those able to reason with rigor
it ignores it, as a matter wholly outside religion
why: Ibn Rushd argues from verses such as "So learn a lesson, O ye who have eyes!" (59:2) that the law calls for reflection, so demonstrative study is obligatory for those able to do it; truth, he says, does not oppose truth.

es.stem: en su Tratado decisivo (Fasl al-Maqal), ¿qué dice Ibn Rushd (Averroes) que manda la ley religiosa sobre el estudio de la filosofía?
options: lo prohíbe, pues razonar aleja a los creyentes de la fe
lo permite solo a gobernantes y a sus médicos de corte
lo ordena a quienes son capaces de razonar con rigor
lo ignora, por ser un asunto del todo ajeno a la religión
es.why: Ibn Rushd argumenta, con versos como "¡Aprendan la lección, oh ustedes que tienen ojos!" (59:2), que la ley pide reflexionar, así que el estudio demostrativo es obligatorio para quienes pueden hacerlo; la verdad, dice, no se opone a la verdad.

stem: which Sunni school of law, carried west from Medina and Kairouan, became the main legal tradition of North Africa and West Africa?
options: the Hanafi school
the Maliki school
the Shafi'i school
the Hanbali school
why: The school of Malik ibn Anas of Medina, author of the Muwatta, spread through Kairouan and al-Andalus across the Maghreb and along the Saharan trade routes into West Africa.
source: Malik ibn Anas, al-Muwatta; Qadi Iyad, Tartib al-Madarik

es.stem: ¿qué escuela sunita de derecho, llevada al oeste desde Medina y Kairuán, se volvió la principal tradición legal del norte y el oeste de África?
options: la escuela hanafí
la escuela malikí
la escuela shafií
la escuela hanbalí
es.why: La escuela de Malik ibn Anas de Medina, autor del Muwatta, se extendió por Kairuán y al-Ándalus a todo el Magreb y, por las rutas comerciales del Sahara, hasta África occidental.

stem: According to a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, what did the Prophet ﷺ say about his grandson Hasan ibn Ali, and how did Hasan's later dealings with Mu'awiyah bear it out?
why: From the pulpit the Prophet ﷺ called Hasan a sayyid (leader) through whom God might make peace between two great groups of Muslims; after Ali's death Hasan made a treaty with Mu'awiyah and stepped aside, ending the fighting. Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Peacemaking.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Peacemaking (Kitab al-Sulh)

rubric.point: Says the Prophet ﷺ foretold that God might make peace through Hasan between two great groups (parties) of Muslims. Saying only that the Prophet loved or praised Hasan counts as partly.
Says Hasan made peace or a treaty with Mu'awiyah and gave up (stepped aside from) leadership or the caliphate to stop the bloodshed. 'He fought and won' does not count.
Mentions that the Prophet called him a sayyid (leader), or that the year became known as the year of unity ('am al-jama'a) (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: Según un hadiz del Sahih al-Bujari, ¿qué dijo el Profeta ﷺ de su nieto Hasan ibn Ali, y cómo lo confirmó lo que Hasan hizo después con Muawiya?
es.why: Desde el púlpito, el Profeta ﷺ llamó a Hasan un sayyid (líder) por medio del cual Dios podría hacer la paz entre dos grandes grupos de musulmanes; tras la muerte de Ali, Hasan hizo un tratado con Muawiya y se hizo a un lado, poniendo fin a la lucha. Sahih al-Bujari, Libro de la reconciliación.

stem: What work went on in Baghdad around the Bayt al-Hikmah, the House of Wisdom, under Abbasid caliphs such as al-Ma'mun, and what came of it?
why: Scholars, Muslim and non-Muslim (such as the Christian physician Hunayn ibn Ishaq), translated Greek, Syriac, Persian and Sanskrit works into Arabic, from Euclid, Ptolemy, Galen and Aristotle to Indian astronomy and numbers; Muslim scholars then studied, corrected and built on them. Ibn al-Nadim, al-Fihrist. Historians debate what the House itself was.

rubric.point: Says books were translated into Arabic, naming at least one source language or tradition (Greek, Syriac, Persian, Sanskrit/Indian). 'They collected books' without translation counts as partly.
Says scholars went on to study, correct or build on this learning in a field such as mathematics, medicine, astronomy or philosophy.
Names a figure (Hunayn ibn Ishaq, al-Khwarizmi, al-Kindi) or a translated author (Aristotle, Galen, Euclid, Ptolemy), or notes historians debate what the House itself was (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: ¿Qué trabajo se hacía en Bagdad en torno a la Bayt al-Hikmah, la Casa de la Sabiduría, bajo califas abasíes como al-Mamún, y qué salió de él?
es.why: Sabios musulmanes y no musulmanes (como el médico cristiano Hunayn ibn Ishaq) tradujeron al árabe obras griegas, siríacas, persas y sánscritas, desde Euclides, Ptolomeo, Galeno y Aristóteles hasta la astronomía y los números de la India; luego los sabios musulmanes las estudiaron, corrigieron y desarrollaron. Ibn al-Nadim, al-Fihrist. Los historiadores discuten qué era la Casa en sí.
